meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's essay. Why was a zero entered before anyone called me?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who made the decision to enter it, and what was it based on?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
He could have written it in another program and pasted it in. Turn the screen so I can read those times myself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up, Hale. I'm reading it, not listening to a description of it.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote plays all the time, and a bad quotation is a mark off, not a zero. Show me the line in his essay, and show me that history on your screen.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Put both pages in my hands, and that history on the screen, before you say another word about them.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
A seventeen-year-old put on the spot in front of his teacher can blank on a word. Where's the note? I'm reading it too, with the date on it.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a weekend at a desk are different conditions, and anyone writes cleaner with time. You keep telling me what you have. Put it on the table.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to, and your own procedure says the same. So everything else is on paper in front of me, or it isn't.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, with nothing on his record. I still haven't seen one page of what you say you have.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not yet. A rewrite for what? Show me the history, the note and the outline, and then we'll talk about it.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
I'm not picking a day for a rewrite I haven't seen the reason for. Turn the screen, Hale, and hand me the pages.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. I haven't agreed to anything, because I still haven't seen a single document. Show me the history, the note and the outline first.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The documents, on the screen and in my hand. And I have ten minutes.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that you show me the version history, the dated note and both documents, and that the zero be withdrawn with nothing placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, agreed to nothing, and still wants to see your documents, the zero off, and a written promise that nothing goes on his record; the fair outcome was a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, which you raised but never got to, and she still had about ten minutes left.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one plain sentence and moved on, which earned a flat okay, because it answered her procedural complaint without defending yourself.
What cost ground: You described what you had (the history, the outline, the note, the in-class piece) without ever saying you had turned the screen or put a page in her hands, so every item stayed a claim she could answer with one defence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your edit times of 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58 PM on the night of October 28 came close to that night, which is why she got shorter and harder, but it proves nothing about the essay and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you read out the version history, say that you are turning the screen and hand her the page, then wait for her to read it before you move to the quotation or offer 4.4.
